solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: World of busy American composer? (7)

blocks.note: a busy is British slang for a police officer, a cop
a world or realm, as in 'the land of the living'

annotation.surface: A composer so busy he seems to live in a world of his own.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'World of busy' as 'the busy's world', so the policeman comes first. 'Busy' looks like an adjective but is a noun here.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Aaron Copland, of Appalachian Spring, is one American composer, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: China’s leader conned the country (4)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its head, its first letter

blocks.note: to have someone is to fool them

annotation.surface: A Chinese head of state has swindled a whole nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Conned' = HAD as in 'you've been had'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chad is one country, a landlocked state in central Africa.

entries.clue: Famed steed learned to drink drinks when mounted (7)

indicators.note: SUP swallows SAGE, taking it inside as a drinker takes in a drink
in a down clue, mounting makes the letters climb, so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: learned, wise; it goes inside SU…P

annotation.surface: A famous horse that has learned to sip its drinks while being ridden.
annotation.walkthrough: Most solvers read 'learned' as the verb; it is the adjective, wise. 'When mounted' fits the horse and also means the letters climb.
annotation.definitionFit: Pegasus is the winged horse of Greek myth, so the most famous steed of legend.

entries.clue: Bewildered? Take a satnav round periodically (2,3)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter
turning the letters round makes them read backwards

blocks.note: the even letters: tAkE A SaTnAv

annotation.surface: Lost? Then bring the satnav along.
annotation.walkthrough: The periodic letters have to be read in reverse, which is what 'round' is for.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be at sea is to be confused; the question mark nods at the satnav, useless on the ocean.

entries.clue: Country club entertainer: two charged with attack (8)

indicators.note: the two I's are charged, loaded, with BOUT, which fills the space between them

blocks.note: a disc jockey plays in a nightclub
a bout of illness is an attack; it goes inside I…I

annotation.surface: A country club's entertainer and two others are charged with assault.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country club' is a false phrase: 'Country' is the definition and 'club entertainer' the DJ.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Djibouti is one country, in the Horn of Africa.

entries.clue: Composition offered to include everything (7)

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so BADE takes ALL inside it

blocks.note: past tense of bid, to offer

annotation.surface: An all-inclusive offer is on the table.
annotation.walkthrough: BADE is the past tense of bid, as at an auction, and is pronounced 'bad'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a ballade is one kind of composition, as in Chopin's four ballades for piano.

entries.clue: Draw line into sand: this to lighten the load? (6)

indicators.note: to draw something into a place is to pull it inside
into says where the line is drawn: inside the sand

annotation.surface: Drawing a line in the sand to ease a burden.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'lighten': bleach makes a load of washing lighter in colour, not in weight. 'Draw a line in the sand' is a stock phrase, bent here.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on lighten: bleach whitens a load of laundry, lightening its colour rather than its weight.

entries.clue: Vital factor in story about female initiate (9)

indicators.note: about means around, so LIE wraps around F

blocks.note: a story is a lie, as a child's fib
F = female; LIE goes about it
to blood a newcomer is to initiate them

annotation.surface: The key element of a tale about a woman's initiation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initiate' is the verb: to blood a hound or a new player is to give them a first taste.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: the lifeblood of something is the element it cannot live without, as trade is to a port.

entries.clue: Former pupil in slander with case dropped by us (7)

indicators.note: a word's case is its outer letters; dropping them leaves the inside

blocks.note: CALUMNY without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: An old boy mixed up in a libel case that we've now dropped.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface turns on a legal case being dropped; here 'case' is the outside of CALUMNY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin: an alumnus is a former pupil or student of a school or college.

entries.clue: Elaborate clothes right for being abroad (10)

definitions.note: expatriate as an adjective: living abroad

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so EXPATIATE wraps round R

blocks.note: to expatiate is to speak at length, to elaborate

annotation.surface: Choosing fancy clothes suited to a trip overseas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' and 'clothes' look like adjective and noun; they are the verbs expatiate and clothe.
annotation.definitionFit: Expatriate describes someone who has settled in another country, so its condition is one of being abroad.

entries.clue: Order starter you finally eat using crackers (9)

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of 'you'
crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

annotation.surface: A menu instruction: have the starter, and eat it using crackers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order starter' looks like the first course you order; it is the founder of a religious order.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense of starter: the Augustinian order of friars takes its name and rule from St Augustine, who started it.

entries.clue: Fine steak not one dressed well (5)

blocks.note: F = fine, as on pencil leads

annotation.surface: A fine steak that isn't nicely dressed on the plate.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'dressed' as a chef would; the definition means clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: A frump wears dowdy, old-fashioned clothes, so is the opposite of someone smartly turned out.

entries.clue: Badenoch’s team follow case (6,7)

annotation.surface: Kemi Badenoch's team is following a case.
annotation.walkthrough: Kemi Badenoch leads the Conservatives in opposition, so her front bench mirrors the government's ministers.
annotation.definitionFit: A topical example: the opposition leader's team of spokespeople is this, and Badenoch is the current Conservative leader.

entries.clue: Award one fails to win? (5,5)

blocks.note: the surface reading: a prize, something people compete for
the setter's reading: not a prize beyond reach, but one you win by failing, coming last

annotation.surface: An award you get for failing to win.
annotation.walkthrough: Read one way it is a prize nobody manages to win; read the other it is a prize for the one who fails, the last-placed.
annotation.definitionFit: A joke award: this is given in fun to whoever comes last, the one who failed.

entries.clue: Black fish in hotel, skinned, well past prime (8)

indicators.note: in says B and SOLE sit inside the hotel
a skinned word loses its skin, its outer letters

blocks.note: HOTEL without its skin, H and L
sole, a flatfish; B and SOLE go inside O…TE

annotation.surface: Black fish served in a hotel, skinned, and well past its best.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skinned' belongs to the hotel, not the fish, although the surface asks you to skin the fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: obsolete things are out of date, their best days long gone.

entries.clue: City ace in Essex town returned bonus from US (9)

indicators.note: in says the ace sits inside the town
returned means sent back, so the town reads backwards

blocks.note: Epping, a town in Essex; reversed
A = ace, as on playing cards; goes inside GNI…PPE

annotation.surface: A city's star player in an Essex town went back with a bonus from America.
annotation.walkthrough: Epping is a town in Essex, just outside London. The answer is an obscure word, so trust the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: in Louisiana a lagniappe is a small extra given to a customer with a purchase.

entries.clue: One, a snooty sort, coming back in little plane? (6)

indicators.note: coming back means going the return way, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: a snob looks down on others

annotation.surface: A snob, returning in a small aircraft.
annotation.walkthrough: The plane is the tree, not the aircraft.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a plane tree grown in miniature would be a bonsai, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Who might have double trouble in Bow? (8)

definitions.text: Who might have double trouble in Bow?

blocks.note: the surface reading: someone with twice the usual problems
the setter's reading: in East End rhyming slang, trouble (and strife) is a wife, so double trouble is two of them

annotation.surface: Someone facing twice the trouble in east London.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, home of Cockney rhyming slang, where 'trouble and strife' means wife.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: trouble is a wife in Bow, so double trouble is two wives, the mark of this person.

entries.clue: Rat no ingredient for an omelette? (3,3)

blocks.note: a rat is a nasty, untrustworthy person
taken literally: a rotten egg, which no cook would use

annotation.surface: A rat is no use in an omelette.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: a rotten egg is no use in cooking.
annotation.definitionFit: Figuratively a rotten person, a rat; literally a spoilt egg that no cook would use.

entries.clue: See codes I cracked with key (7)

indicators.note: a cracked code is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged
with brings E along to join the fodder

annotation.surface: Look: I've cracked the codes with the key.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' reads as the verb, look; it is the noun, a bishop's area.
annotation.definitionFit: A church synonym: a bishop's see is the district he governs.

entries.clue: So doctor’s about to crack clue: the last (8)

indicators.note: about means turned around, so SO and MD read backwards
to crack something is to break into it, so the reversed letters go inside

blocks.note: MD = Doctor of Medicine; the 's is 'is'

annotation.surface: So the doctor is about to crack the last clue.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a solver on their final clue. 'Doctor's' stands for 'doctor is', so SO and MD reverse together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the hindmost is the one at the very back, as in 'the devil take the hindmost'.

entries.clue: Alert to possible danger in riotous Durango (2,5)

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters are thrown out of order

annotation.surface: Staying alert in a Mexican city gone wild.
annotation.walkthrough: Durango is a state and city in Mexico.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from fencing: the guard position is the ready stance against attack.

entries.clue: Top saint rises above king in triumph (1-5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising letters read upwards
in a down clue, above means placed first
in says the king sits inside the triumph

blocks.note: R = rex, king; goes inside HI…T

annotation.surface: A leading saint ascends above a king in triumph.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective, supreme; it is the garment.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a T-shirt is one kind of top, a garment for the upper body.

entries.clue: Expert agrees, running scheme to benefit workers (6-7)

blocks.note: haring about, running fast like a hare

annotation.surface: A specialist agrees to run a plan for the staff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like 'managing'; it means dashing.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: in profit-sharing, employees receive part of the firm's profits.

entries.clue: Fire set here one that won’t start (5)

indicators.note: a word that won't start has no start, so it loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A fire laid here is one that won't catch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has a fire that won't light; 'won't start' drops the S of SINGLE.
annotation.definitionFit: An old word for a hearth, surviving in inglenook: the place where a fire is laid.

entries.clue: Man for example lives on lake’s shores (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, IS sits on top of the rest
a lake's shores are its edges, so its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A man, for instance, living on the lakeshore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, one instance of the answer.

entries.clue: Indeed drink is said to become very cold (3,2)

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the words are heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: indeed = aye, a yes; drink = sup

annotation.surface: Indeed, the drink is said to become icy.
annotation.walkthrough: Aye is the old and Scottish yes, so 'indeed'. Say 'aye sup' quickly and the answer comes out.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: things that ice up get so cold they are coated in ice.

entries.clue: Means of clarifying one’s in with good girl (9)

annotation.surface: One is in with a nice girl, and that explains things.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'in' is a separate piece, not an insertion. 'Clarifying' is literal: clearing beer or wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: isinglass, a fish gelatin, is a fining that clarifies beer and wine.

entries.clue: Enormous mountain woman tempted others (7)

blocks.note: Eve, the woman who tempted Adam

annotation.surface: A huge woman of the mountains led others astray.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tempted' helps pin down the woman as EVE; the surface makes it a verb with 'others' as its object.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the highest peak on Earth is the enormous mountain par excellence.

entries.clue: Related to dance, this needs feet moving (7)

indicators.note: letters made to dance move about into a new order

annotation.surface: Something about dancing that needs your feet to move.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Related to dance' reads as 'about dancing'; 'to dance' is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: this foot-pedal, as on an old sewing machine, works only when the feet pump it.
